IdempotencyKeyHeader.description: Makes the request safe to repeat. A retry with the same key and the same request answers the first response again, marked `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, for 24 hours; the same key with another request is 422 `idempotency-key-reuse`, and a retry while the first request is still running is 409 `idempotency-in-progress`. A first attempt that ended in an error can be repeated.
IdempotencyKeyHeader.name: Idempotency-Key

IdempotencyKeyRequiredHeader.description: Required: makes the batch safe to repeat. A retry with the same key and the same request answers the first response again, marked `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, for 24 hours; the same key with another request is 422 `idempotency-key-reuse`, and a retry while the first request is still running is 409 `idempotency-in-progress`. A first attempt that ended in an error can be repeated.
IdempotencyKeyRequiredHeader.name: Idempotency-Key

IdempotencyKeySecretHeader.description: Makes the request safe to repeat in the sense that it never takes effect twice. The response contains a secret, which is shown once and never stored, so a retry with the same key is answered 409 `secret-not-replayable` (with the status and the `Location` of the first answer, so that the result can be found, read or revoked) instead of replaying it. The same key with another request is 422 `idempotency-key-reuse`. A first attempt that ended in an error can be repeated.
IdempotencyKeySecretHeader.name: Idempotency-Key

BadRequest.description: The request is malformed: an invalid query parameter or header, or a body that is not JSON.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the current state: a uniqueness conflict, `idempotency-in-progress`, `secret-not-replayable`, `feature-not-enabled` or, for a principal, `name-reserved`, `external-ref-reserved` or `address-reserved` (the value belongs to a deleted principal that is not purged yet); the `code` member says which.

Gone.description: The sync token is not usable any more (`sync-token-expired`); start over without `since`.

NotFound.description: The resource does not exist or is not visible to the token.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The request body is larger than the limit.

PreconditionFailed.description: `If-Match` or `If-None-Match` does not hold for the current version of the resource. `If-None-Match: *` fails for every name that exists, including the name of a deleted principal that is not purged yet (a write without it answers 409 `name-reserved` for that name).

EventView.description:
An event as the management API and MCP show it.

The metadata members are set by the server on read and ignored on write. The event fields of a write are merged
into the stored event like a JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) for the members of the event: a field with a value
replaces the stored one, an absent field keeps it and a field that is `null` removes it. A member that is an object
or a list replaces the stored one as a whole (`recurrence`, `organizer`, `alarms`: a `recurrence` with only
`exdates` drops the stored rule); attendees are matched by address and keep the parameters the write does not state.

Selects an override instance of a recurring event; absent addresses the master component. `null` is the

The revision number; the server raises it on significant changes when the client does not. `null` is the

required.description:
Whether the calendar is **required** for the people the grant reaches: the grantee, or the members of a grantee
group. They cannot remove it from their calendar home, so a `DELETE` of its collection from a client is refused
(403, `DAV:need-privileges` naming `DAV:unbind`) instead of hiding the calendar for good; a binding that was
hidden before (also one hidden before its owner joined the group) is shown again. Without the flag (the default) the
calendar is optional: a client that deletes the collection hides it, and the binding can be restored through
`POST …/bindings/{binding}/restore`. The flag belongs to the grant, so a `PUT` that leaves it out sets it to `false`
(send it on every `PUT`); it has no effect while the grant is not accepted (API grants always are). Only a tenant
token sets or clears it: a principal's token is refused with 403 when it asks for `true`, and a grant it puts keeps
the flag it has.

HomeBindingView.description:
A calendar in the home of a principal, as the management API lists it: the **binding** through which the principal's
calendar apps see the calendar, whether or not the principal removed it from the home.

A principal who deletes a shared calendar (a group calendar, a managed one, a calendar of someone else) in a calendar
app hides the binding; the calendar is not deleted and the grant stays. `hidden` says so, and
`POST …/bindings/{binding}/restore` shows the calendar again. `required` says that the principal cannot remove the
calendar at all (a grant with the `required` flag reaches them).

Role.description:
Participation role of an attendee (`ROLE`).

Values:
- `chair`: `CHAIR`.
- `req_participant`: `REQ-PARTICIPANT` (the default).
- `opt_participant`: `OPT-PARTICIPANT`.
- `non_participant`: `NON-PARTICIPANT`.

ScheduleAgent.description:
Who performs scheduling for an attendee (`SCHEDULE-AGENT`, RFC 6638).

Values:
- `server`: `SERVER` (the default): the server delivers scheduling messages.
- `client`: `CLIENT`: the client takes care of it; the server never delivers.
- `none`: `NONE`: no scheduling messages at all.

auto_add_invitations.description: Whether invitations are added to internal attendees' calendars automatically.

external.description: Policy for attendees outside the tenant.

external_allowlist.description: Lowercase domains (`example.org`) and addresses (`anna@example.org`) allowed under `allowlist`.

inbound_methods.description: iTIP methods accepted by the inbound endpoint (`reply` only unless `request` or `cancel` are enabled).

suppress_duplicate_copies.description: Give attendees who already have a binding to the organizer's calendar an inbox item instead of a copy.

SenderSettings.description: Sender identity of outgoing iMIP mail (`"{organizer} via {display name}" <local_part@domain>`).

display_name.description: Name shown after "via"; the tenant display name when unset.

domain.description: Sender domain; mail cannot be sent for the tenant while unset.

local_part.description: Local part of the sender address.

auto_accept.description: Skip the notification step: invitations are accepted automatically.

enabled.description: Whether clients may share calendars (CalendarServer sharing).

allowed_components.description: Component types calendars of the tenant may hold.

auto_create_personal_calendar.description: Create a personal calendar when a user principal is created.

busy_text.description:
The summary of the busy blocks of busy-mode feeds (PLAN 2.13), the same text in every language: "In a meeting",
"Nicht verfügbar". It overrides the `feed_busy` template, and `busy_text_by_locale` overrides it for the languages
that map names. Unset (the default) the summary is that template of the tenant's theme in the language of the feed's
owner ("Busy", "Beschäftigt"). One to 100 characters, surrounding white space is removed; control characters, line
and paragraph separators and invisible or bidirectional formatting characters are refused.

busy_text_by_locale.description:
The summary of the busy blocks of busy-mode feeds in each language the tenant names, as a map from a language tag
(`de`, `en-GB`) to the text: `{"de": "Nicht verfügbar", "en": "Unavailable"}`. The reader of a feed gets the text of
its own language, which is the language of the feed's owner (the principal's locale, else the tenant's): the tag is
looked up as it is and then without its last subtag (`de-AT` finds `de`; `zh-Hant-TW` tries `zh-Hant`, then `zh`),
and the first text found wins. A language the map does not name gets `busy_text` when that is set, and else the
`feed_busy` template of the theme. Every text follows the rules of `busy_text`; at most 20 languages. Empty (the
default) names none. A merge patch changes one language with its tag and removes it with `null`; a document that
writes one tag twice in different spellings (`de-DE` and `de_de`) is refused.

dav_base_url.description: Base URL of the DAV service when it differs from the public base URL.

feeds_enabled.description: Whether subscription feeds can be created and served.

group_default_access.description: Access members of a group get on the group's calendars.

locale.description: Default locale for mail and pages.

login_address_is_cua.description: Whether the login address counts as a calendar user address of the principal.

mcp_enabled.description: Whether the MCP server is available to the tenant.

public_base_url.description: Per-tenant override of `server.public_base_url` for links in mail and feeds.

schema_version.description: Version of this document's schema; readers ignore fields they do not know.

theme.description:
Name of the template theme. Unset (the default) means the theme the deployment names in
`templates.default_theme`, which is `default` unless the operator chose another: a tenant that has no
branding of its own follows the deployment, and a tenant that names a theme keeps it whatever the deployment
chooses later. Serialized as `null` when unset, like the other optional settings.

timezone.description: Default time zone for principals without one.

TenantStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of a tenant.

Values:
- `active`: The tenant is in service.
- `suspended`: Logins and tokens of the tenant are refused; data is kept.

TenantView.description: A tenant as the management API shows it.

slug.description: The immutable slug used in DAV and API paths.

updated_at.description: When the tenant was last changed.

version.description: The optimistic concurrency counter; the `ETag` is derived from it.

TenantWrite.description: The body of a tenant `PUT`: create or replace.

login_domain.description: The domain of `name@login_domain` logins, unique across tenants.

TokenKind.description:
The kind of an API token (`api_tokens.kind`).

Values:
- `system`: Operates on tenants only (`system:tenants`); never reads calendar data. Not bound to a tenant.
- `tenant`: Acts as administrator of one tenant within its scopes.
- `principal`: Acts as exactly one principal, through the same authorization as DAV.

Transparency.description:
Whether an event blocks time (`TRANSP`).

Values:
- `opaque`: `OPAQUE` (the default): counts as busy.
- `transparent`: `TRANSPARENT`: does not block time.

events.description: The event types to receive; an empty list receives nothing.

include_details.description: Whether payloads carry details such as summary and times (default `false`: thin payloads).

url.description: The target URL. Must be https; the egress policy is applied at registration and on every delivery.

WebhookCreated.description: A freshly created webhook. The signing secret is shown only here.

WebhookSecretRotated.description:
The result of rotating a signing secret: the new secret is shown once; the previous one keeps signing
alongside it until the retry window of pending deliveries has passed.

WebhookView.description: A webhook subscription as the management API shows it. The secret is never part of it.

disabled_reason.description: Why the subscription was disabled automatically.

events.description: The event types the subscription receives.

failure_count.description: How many deliveries failed in a row.

include_details.description: Whether payloads carry details such as summary and times.

secret_rotated_at.description: When the signing secret was last rotated.

updated_at.description: When the subscription was last changed.

version.description: The optimistic concurrency counter; the `ETag` is derived from it.

bearerAuth.description: An API token in the `Authorization: Bearer` header. System tokens manage tenants, tenant tokens administer one tenant within their scopes, principal tokens act as their principal. Tokens are never accepted in URLs or cookies.

info.description:
The management API of Davhaven: provisioning of tenants, principals and memberships, credentials and client configuration, calendars and grants, managed calendar objects with batch upsert, changes feeds, webhooks, provider accounts, audit events, outbox inspection and the inbound iTIP endpoint for mail gateways.

**Conventions.** Paths use the immutable natural keys (tenant slug, principal name, calendar slug, external key). JSON is snake_case, timestamps are RFC 3339 in UTC. Mutable resources return an `ETag` derived from their `version`; `PUT` creates or replaces, `PATCH` takes a JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396), `If-Match` fails with 412, and deleting tenants, principals and calendars requires `If-Match` (428). Lists are cursor pages (`limit`, `cursor`, `next_cursor`, a relative `Link: rel=next`). Every `POST` accepts an `Idempotency-Key` (required for batch upserts); a replayed response carries `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, and a response that contains a secret is never stored or replayed: the retry is answered 409 `secret-not-replayable` with the status and `Location` of the first answer. Errors are RFC 9457 problem documents with a stable `code`; 429 and 503 carry `Retry-After`. Every operation lists the scopes a token needs in `x-required-scope` (any one of them suffices).

**Compatibility.** The API is versioned by its path; changes within `v1` are additive: new operations, new optional members and new values of enumerations, problem codes included. Clients must ignore members they do not know and tolerate enumeration values they do not know: the enumerations of this document list the values of this release, and a generated client has to be configured to keep an unknown value (see `docs/api.md`). Deprecations are announced with `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers.

post.description:
The token is in the response and nowhere else; store it now.

A token mints tokens whose scopes are a subset of its own, and a minted token never outlives its minter. **One
exception**: the `mcp:*` scopes, which a tenant token cannot hold itself. A tenant token with `credentials:write` may
put them on a principal token for a **service principal**, because the machine identity of an assistant needs exactly
these and `credentials:write` is already the power to act as any principal of the tenant that can act (it mints app
passwords as well). Every other scope of the token still has to be one the minter holds. The token then acts **as**
that principal: it sees and writes the calendars the principal owns or is granted, nothing else. For a user the subset
rule stays, so MCP scopes reach a user only from the operator (`davhaven admin principal-token`). Tokens with `mcp:*`
scopes need a tenant that switched MCP on (`409 feature-not-enabled` otherwise) and an expiry within
`security.max_mcp_token_days`. Every minting is audited (`token.created`).

Credentials, RSVP tokens and shares are revoked at once and the principal disappears; it is purged after the
retention period, or immediately with `purge=true`. Requires `If-Match`.

put.description:
Declarative provisioning: sending the same body twice changes nothing. The kind of an existing principal cannot
change.

**Deleted principals.** A principal that was deleted without `purge=true` is hidden (it is not listed and not found
by `external_ref`), but its name, its `external_ref` and its addresses stay reserved until it is purged
(`retention.principal_purge_days`, or `DELETE …?purge=true` before). The answers are fixed so that a client that
provisions principals can tell them from a conflict with a live principal: `If-None-Match: *` for the name of a
deleted principal answers **412** (`precondition-failed`, exactly as for a name that exists, with no hint about
the hidden principal); a write **without** it for that name answers **409** `name-reserved`; a create or a replace
whose `external_ref` collides with a deleted principal answers **409** `external-ref-reserved`, and one whose
address collides with it **409** `address-reserved`. Purge the hidden principal or wait for the retention period,
then repeat the request. A collision with a **live** principal is the plain 409 `conflict`.

The bindings of the principal's home that their calendar apps can list, **hidden ones included**: a principal who deletes a
shared calendar in a calendar app hides its binding, and `hidden` says so (`?hidden=true` lists only those). `required` says
that the principal cannot remove the calendar (a grant with the `required` flag reaches them). A calendar the principal can
no longer reach (a removed group member, a revoked grant) is not listed, and a binding exists from the principal's first
listing of the home on, so the list holds the bindings created so far. `slug` is the last segment of the DAV path and the
`{binding}` of the restore path. Bindings are ordered by id.

touched, so nothing else needs repair. Restoring a binding that is visible changes nothing and answers 200 as well, so a

as an unknown one does. The restoration is audited (`binding.restored`). A binding has no `ETag`: it cannot be fetched or
changed on its own.

put.description:
Creates the grant or replaces the access level of an existing one. Groups are expanded dynamically: members
who join later gain access, members who leave lose it. A **service principal** (the machine identity of an assistant
or an integration, which holds principal tokens for the API and MCP) is granted like a user; client sharing
(`CS:share`) and principal search do not offer it. Resources are refused (422), and so is the owner of the calendar,
except a **group that owns its calendar**: it may be granted that calendar to mark it `required` for its members. That
grant adds no access (the members have the group's default access already), so its access is `read`, and only a tenant
token puts it.

**`required`.** A grant with `required: true` makes the calendar mandatory for everybody it reaches (the grantee, or the
members of a grantee group): a calendar app that deletes the collection is refused with 403 (`DAV:need-privileges`,
`DAV:unbind`) instead of hiding it for good, and bindings that were hidden before come back, including those of people
who join the group later. A grant without the flag is optional: deleting the collection hides it, and
`POST …/bindings/{binding}/restore` shows it again. `PUT` replaces the grant, so a body without `required` makes the
grant optional: **send the flag on every `PUT`.** Only a tenant token sets or clears it; a principal's token is refused
with 403 when it asks for `true`, a grant it puts keeps the flag the grant has, and it cannot remove a required grant. A
client's `CS:share` never sets the flag and cannot change or remove a grant that has it.

parameters.description: The name of the user, group or service principal that is granted access.
parameters.name: grantee

put.description:
The body is merged into the stored event like a JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) for the members of the event: a field
with a value replaces the stored one, a field that is absent keeps it and a field that is `null` is removed
(`location: null` clears the location). A member that is an object or a list replaces the stored one as a whole
(`recurrence`, `organizer`, `alarms`: a `recurrence` with only `exdates` drops the stored rule); attendees are
matched by address. `uid` and `start` cannot be removed and refuse `null` (422 at the pointer of the member);
`null` for `recurrence_id` and `sequence` is the same as leaving them out. Unknown properties, alarms and `X-`
properties are preserved.
`If-Match` takes the content ETag of the event.
